hypothesis: Iter 81 = per-patient glucose baseline + off-manifold robustness, targeting the iter-80 gate REGRESSION (glucose_mape 0.20->1.45, overall_mape 0.37, skill_vs_persistence(real) negative every marker). Local diagnosis of the landed iter-80 model refuted the 'amplitude overshoot' read: (a) the benchmark's glucose eval is a FASTING-WINDOW baseline test — all 24 synthetic users have meals only in the calibration window (90/210/330 min) and a flat post-meal eval window (510-690), with per-user fasting glucose a uniform staircase 60->118 mg/dL; persistence scores glucose_mape ~0.009. (b) The model CANNOT represent low baselines: its achievable fasting glucose over the calibration-reachable embedding region floors at ~98 mg/dL (downward authority ~0) because the structural clearance term -Sg*(G-Gb) pulled toward a HARDCODED Gb=95 — so ~2/3 of benchmark users (60-97) were unrepresentable, and the model over-predicted (108-141) vs flat-low truth, losing to persistence. iter-80's added amplitude made it strictly worse. FIX (MetabolicModule): a small embedding head emits a per-patient baseline offset b_emb (z-score), so clearance pulls toward Gb = 95 + NORM_SCALE*b_emb — giving the embedding DIRECT linear authority over the fasting setpoint (SetpointHead idea applied surgically to the existing term; NO head swap, respecting the iter-72 scar that swapping metabolic heads wrecked the ACTH coupling). tanh-bounded ±1.5σ (Gb~50-140); final layer zero-init => b_emb=0 at start => Gb=95 byte-identical to iter-80. Also helps the slow post-meal decay (glucose now relaxes toward the patient's true low baseline before the eval window). ROBUSTNESS (committed alongside, cfaabb1): (i) calibration embedding leash ||emb||<=3 — iter-80 calibration walked ||emb|| to ~10.8 (9x off the trained manifold ~1.15) where the unbounded integration detonated glucose to ~18,000 mg/dL; (ii) physiological state clamp at NORM_CENTER±20*NORM_SCALE, straight-through (forward bounded, gradient identity) so early training is not starved. CONFIG HELD BYTE-IDENTICAL to iter 79/80 (params unchanged): the baseline mechanism is trained by the existing per-patient trajectory/cohort signals (teacher varies Gb at sigma=0.15, full_body randomize_params), so the benchmark is attributable to exactly the b_emb + clamp/leash changes.
expectedEffect: PRIMARY (the iter-80 regression): (1) glucose_mape drops sharply from 1.45 — the model can now calibrate each patient's fasting baseline (60-118) instead of flooring at ~98, and the eval window is fasting so a correct flat baseline should approach persistence (0.009); (2) glucose skill_vs_persistence(real) turns less negative / positive as the baseline mismatch closes; (3) overall_weighted_mape recovers toward the iter-79 ~0.08. WATCH: (4) mid-range users (Gb 82-110, ~half) should improve most — the teacher varies Gb at sigma=0.15 (~82-110 at 1sigma), so b_emb learns authority there; the EXTREME users (60-80, 110-118 ~2.5sigma) may lag if training under-samples them — if so, widen randomize_params Gb spread next iter (the obvious follow-up, held out here for clean attribution). (5) No fasting/acute regression expected from the clamp (in-distribution no-op, verified delta=0) or the leash (||emb||<=3 is ~2.6x the trained norm). RISKS: (R1) b_emb authority may be partial if the trained glucose SpeciesHead keeps fighting toward 95 (local cheap-confirm on the iter-80 ckpt reached Gb=60->84.5 at the trained Sg; the optimizer can raise Sg and relax the head with the b_emb signal present) — partial baseline tracking still improves the gate substantially. (R2) amplitude vs flatness is NOT a conflict in this eval (eval window is fasting); dose-response amplitude is exercised in the calibration window + separate signals.
